Last week, news broke that hackers had stolen $6.3 billion from wallets on Binance, the most popular cryptocurrency exchange in the world. The company was able to freeze about nearly $3 billion of it, but the attack quickly made headlines, and rightfully so, as the largest financial heist in human history.

At the time, I suspected, along with security researcher Christopher Lopez and plenty of others, that this could have very well started on a Mac. As Lopez pointed out, the $1.5 billion Bybit heist last year also began on a developer’s Mac. On top of that, Macs are hugely popular among DevOps engineers and crypto folks, and they’ve been on the receiving end of a steady stream of malware and social engineering campaigns over the past few years.

I can now say any suspicions that this heist originated on Mac were right. I’m still in a state of shock. Dazed not by the amount stolen, but how the said hackers did so using the same ol’ social engineering tricks they’ve been using for years. No sophisticated multi-milllion dollar underground zero-day here.

Yesterday, Binance published a more detailed breakdown of the attack. The company never actually says “Mac,” but the malware it published targeted /opt/homebrew, which is where Homebrew lives on Apple silicon Macs. In other words, this was almost certainly an M-series MacBook.

The attack basically transpired in two steps.

According to Binance, in June this year, a DevOps engineer working on Wallet searched for an AI coding tool and downloaded a malicious clone of the Homebrew installer in Google Search. Binance claims it caught it early and stopped any damage. However, what it didn’t know was that it allowed the attackers to learn which employees worked on its wallets. This was phase 1.

Fast forward a few months to September, a different engineer who, you guessed it, worked on wallets for Binance, was lured into a fake job interview. As these sort of social engineering attacks normally go, they told to run a coding “assignment” on their work computer. This was not caught by Binance security, and on October 29, the world learned that hackers (now widely speculated as North Korean hackers) walked off with billions.

Of course, most of what we know so far comes directly from Binance, so if you’re looking for more details on exactly how this happened, you’ll likely be left empty-handed.

It’s important to note here though, none of these two attack vectors are new. Back in early 2025, I wrote about fake Homebrew ads at the top of Google Search pushing Atomic Stealer to Mac users. Binance only says the engineer found his installer through “a search engine.” Of course, I can’t confirm it was a sponsored ad, but if history tells us anything…

This is a rather uncomfortable situation for Apple to be in. The largest financial heist in history happen on Mac last week, though to be fair, there’s no security feature that can stop a developer from running a script he wants to run.

Sure, the Terminal paste warnings introduced in macOS 26.4 could have helped here. But realistically, if someone’s convinced they’re doing a coding test for a job they really want, a warning pop-up probably isn’t going to stop them.

I’m having Christopher Lopez (@L0Psec) a professional macOS reverse engineer back on the Security Bite Podcast this week to talk about the Binance situation with me. Follow the show so you don’t miss that.

The Fitbit Edge is Google’s latest launch, and it sits between the $99 Fitbit Air that was released earlier this year and the Pixel Watch 5, Google’s top-tier smartwatch. It’s $180, with a bright screen, built-in GPS, and a comfortable, compact design.

One of the things we do with every new device that lands on our desk here at Tom’s Guide is look at how well it does the basics. We look at how good the auto-detection is at picking up a workout, whether the sleep tracking seems about right, and how well it counts our steps.

To do this, we do one of our infamous walk tests, where we strap a device to each wrist and manually count every step using the kind of clicker tool you’d spot a bouncer at a nightclub holding. Sure, our neighbours wonder what we’re up to, but it’s all in the name of good content.

This week, I decided to see how the $180 Fitbit Edge compared to Apple’s smartest smartwatch — the $800 Apple Watch Ultra 4. Read on to find out which device came out on top, and check out our Fitbit Edge review and Apple Watch Ultra 4 review here.

As always, let's start with how these devices count your steps. Both trackers count steps using an internal accelerometer that measures arm swing. Each swing counts for two steps, and it doesn’t matter whether you wear your watch on your dominant or non-dominant hand. Whether you walk with your hands in your pockets or holding a cup of coffee, the accelerometer should still measure your body’s movement.

As with all the best Apple Watches, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 still doesn’t tell you the number of steps you’ve taken during a specific workout; instead, you see an overall number of steps throughout the day, which you can now pin to your home screen. This is probably because steps aren’t actually that useful a metric beyond a certain point, but annoying for me when writing these articles. For this comparison, I downloaded a third-party Pedometer+ app onto my Apple Watch.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

As you can see from the results, the Fitbit Edge was astonishingly close to the actual number of steps I took, only counting an extra eight over the course of my walk. The Apple Watch Ultra 4, on the other hand, overcounted by 51 steps.

It’s important to point out here that 51 steps don’t make the Apple Watch Ultra 4 inaccurate in any way. The average person takes 2,000 steps a mile, so an extra 51 steps is nothing.

Likewise, it's worth noting that these are two very different devices, and probably not options most people would be deciding between. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is like having an extension of your iPhone on your wrist, with an abundance of apps to choose from. It’s designed to be a rugged smartwatch, designed for extreme sports, whereas the Fitbit Edge is a slim fitness tracker, with a focus on daily health tracking.

We’ll continue testing the Fitbit Edge, but it’s impressive to see how accurate its step counting is in this test. Which device would you choose? Let us know in the poll below.

#3350. This Janus Henderson fund manager owns CoreWeave debt — here's why he's sticking with it

CoreWeave can overcome the market's skepticism about its debt.

That isn't the consensus view — some Coreweave debt remains deeply distressed with yields above 15%. But Coreweave should power through this tough stretch, according to John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson.

"It's a little bit of overreacting," Lloyd tells CNBC, referring to the sell-off in Coreweave bonds, which have tanked along with its equity.

Lloyd owns Coreweave 9.75% bonds due in 2031 in the firm's Multi-Sector Income Fund. The yield to maturity on the debt is now 15.97%, a more than 70% jump since its issuance in April. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

"Bond prices are lower, spreads are wider, yields are wider, and I don't see a huge fundamental change in the ecosystem right now that would warrant that, other than their higher cost of financing, which I think they can get creative with," Lloyd added.

CoreWeave has taken on a massive amount of debt to fund its data center buildout. The company has roughly $51.6 billion in total debt, including about $35 billion in notes, bonds and loans.

The market is getting nervous about how CoreWeave will be able to keep financing its data centers, and at what cost. Its stock has tumbled 20% over the past week, while the spread on its five-year credit default swaps is nearly 1,081 basis points — lower than earlier in the session but up 13% week over week. Spreads of 1,000 basis points and above are generally a sign of credit distress.

CoreWeave shares moved roughly 2% higher on Tuesday, after tumbling over the past several days and hitting a 52-week low earlier in the session. Its bond yields and spreads remain highly elevated.

Lloyd believes the selloff is a bump in the road for the neocloud company.

The market has been spooked by the jump in Treasury rates, which pushes up funding costs for companies, he explained. The focus largely turned to companies like CoreWeave that have refinance risk when rates move higher, he said.

CoreWeave leverage is high with a debt-to-equity ratio of 702%, up from 290% a year ago. Moreover, CoreWeave will spend an estimated $36.4 billion on capital expenditures this year against Ebitda of $7.5 billion, according to consensus estimates.

Revenue and Ebitda will ramp up next year, hitting $26.5 billion and $16.7 billion respectively, analysts estimate. But capex will hit $47.9 billion, indicating the company may need to finance its data center buildout with more equity issuance and/or debt.

Lloyd isn't necessarily worried about CoreWeave's ability to finance its capital expenditures, despite the fact that its capex outweighs its free-cash flow.

"Next year … they're going to be generating operating free-cash flow that'll support some of that capex need," he said.

The company can also turn to other methods of funding, like more GPU financing, which will allow it to borrow against its graphics processing units or rental contracts, he noted. In addition, CoreWeave could ask its biggest customers — including Microsoft, Meta Platforms and OpenAI — to increase their prepayments, he added.

"They can probably get creative enough where they don't even need to come to the high-yield market," Lloyd said.

The company also doesn't have any near-term maturities, which means it isn't facing a refinancing risk anytime soon, he added.

Meanwhile the supply/demand dynamic should remain tight across the AI compute landscape. Overall adoption rates within the ecosystem are running above consensus demand curves, he said. Add to that a bottleneck in supply, with chips and memory power sold out, and it's a nice set up for CoreWeave.

"All data point to the business model functioning very, very well," Lloyd said. "CoreWeave is one of the best-in-class at getting data centers up and actually running them," he added, noting that CoreWeave's financials have been improving throughout the year.

Another turning point could come if Anthropic goes forth with an IPO, expected in November, followed by OpenAI. Successful IPOs for the frontier labs could soothe market nerves and help support the neocloud operators.

"You just need more of those data points where people become more comfortable with the AI demand side," Lloyd said.

CoreWeave still needs to convince markets it can handle higher market rates and get through the financing bottlenecks.

Lloyd sees the company making it, albeit with some bumps along the way. The bonds should recover, he says, "just not in that straight line."

#3349. These Are the Best Early Black Friday Deals on Cordless Power Tools

Becca Lewis is home maintenance writer who aims to foster confidence in and inspire DIY enthusiasts at all skill levels.

Becca attended Southern Connecticut State University, where she studied technical theater and design. She has a background in carpentry and fabrication and has worked in specialty shops, using a wide variety of tools and materials, for more than 20 years.

Becca has also written for Angi, where she specializes in creating guides for DIY, home maintenance, and renovations, and she indulges her love of sci-fi and fantasy by writing about entertainment and science for Giant Freakin Robot. She serves on the board of the Good Junk Sanctuary in Portland, Oregon, focusing on community engagement in the DIY and reuse space.

If you have a DIY enthusiast on your list—or if you just want some new tools for your own projects—Black Friday sales are a good time to snag low prices on quality tools. Lots of big box stores are looking to thin out their inventory and make room for next year’s upgrades, so in addition to encouraging a holiday rush, retailers are motivated to price things to move. If you know what to look for, you can get up to 65% off on trusted brands. Here are a few of the best deals out there right now.

If you’re building a new cordless tool set, or updating your battery system, getting a cordless tool set can save you some money because these combos usually include batteries and a charger, which can be the most expensive part of your tool set. Here are a few of the best early Black Friday deals on cordless tool sets.

The Ryobi 6-tool 18-volt combo set is on sale for $199, 33% off its regular price at Home Depot. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, a circular saw, a sawzall, an oscillating multi-tool, a work light, a 1.5-amp-hour battery, a 4-amp-hour battery, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good deal on a trusted home tool brand.

The Ryobi 18-volt drill and driver set is on sale for $99, 34% off its usual price at Home Depot. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, two 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a great starter set because it has the first two tools you need for a cordless kit and it comes with batteries so you can expand your set for cheaper as you develop your skills.

The Ryobi 4-tool, 4-volt project set is on sale for $99, 61% off its typical price at Home Depot. This set comes with a rotary tool, a project light, a glue pen, a mini drill, two rechargeable batteries, a charging cable, a set of starter rotary bits, and three glue sticks. This set is handy for DIY projects that require fine detail, like wood carving, craft projects, or framing pictures.

The DeWalt drill and driver combo set is on sale for $129, 46% off its regular price on Amazon. This set includes a drill, an impact driver, 2 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good deal on a trusted brand for drills and drivers, and a good start for a cordless DIY tool set.

If you have a cordless tool set already and you want to expand your kit, or if you have a DIYer in your life who already has a particular brand of battery and you want to get them something they can use, a single tool deal can be just the thing.

The DeWalt 20-volt compact drill/driver is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. This tool comes with a 20-volt, 2-amp-hour battery and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. It’s a good first tool for a set.

The Milwaukee 18-volt impact wrench is on sale at Home Depot for $199, 68% off its typical price. This tool comes with two 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. This is a good tool for driving bolts through tough materials and for automotive projects.

The DeWalt 20-volt oscillating multi-tool is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 50% off its regular price. This tool comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a charger, so it's ready to use out of the box. This is one of the most versatile cordless tools, allowing you to cut a wide range of materials and use a sanding attachment to do finishing work as well.

The Milwaukee 18-volt tire inflator kit is on sale at Home Depot for $199, 65% off its usual price. This tool comes with two 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger, so it’s ready to go right out of the box. This is an excellent addition to your emergency roadside tool set because you can use it to inflate a car tire with the charged 18-volt batteries.

The DeWalt 12-volt cordless powered ratchet is on sale at Lowe’s for $99, 50% off its typical price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a DeWalt 12-volt battery and charger to use it. This is a good tool for working on cars or for home appliance maintenance because it can fit into tight spaces.

The Makita 18-volt cordless electric 2-inch brad nailer is on sale on Amazon for $336.19, 36% off its regular price. This is a tool only deal, so you’ll need a Makita 18-volt battery and charger to use it. This is a good tool for attaching trim or paneling.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

#3347. Tom Rob Smith Writing Fiction Book Based On West Memphis Three Murder Case — Thessaloniki

British writer Tom Rob Smith led an enlightening Q&A session on the difference between writing prose fiction and writing for the screen this afternoon at the Thessaloniki Film Festival, where he is one of the headline speakers.

During the session, the Emmy winner, best known for the novel Child 44 and the series The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story, also shared his next project: A fiction book based on the West Memphis Three murder case.

“I can tell you because I’m coming right to the end of it,” Smith said when Deadline asked about his next project in Thessaloniki. Related Stories News Magenta TV's Cypriot-Set Thriller 'Brothers' Wasn't Allowed To Shoot In The Country. The Producers Explain Why: "The Reasons Were Political" News How A Mistake In Warner Bros. Contracts Helped Eleven Film & Jack Thorne Land 'Lord Of The Flies' TV Rights -- Thessaloniki

“It’s based on an American crime. A case called the West Memphis Three. It was a killing that took place in 1993. No one was interested in it when it happened. Then HBO made a documentary about it called Paradise Lost. Everyone got involved, including Peter Jackson and Johnny Depp. I’m doing a fictionalized version of that account.” Watch on Deadline

Smith added: “It’s not like Versace, which was a kind of mirror of the case. This is more like Child 44, where you’re taking a real case and telling a story about its ideas rather than the real people.”

Damien Echols, Jessie Misskelley Jr., and Jason Baldwin, known as the West Memphis Three, were convicted as teenagers of the 1993 murders of three 8-year-old boys in West Memphis, Arkansas. The prosecutors at the time said the murders were committed as part of a satanic ritual. Echols was sentenced to death, while Misskelley Jr. and Baldwin were given life sentences. The trio was freed in 2011 after serving 18 years. New DNA evidence excluded the three men from all of the crime scene evidence found at the scene.

Echols, Misskelley Jr., and Baldwin’s received public support from several high-profile figures, including Johnny Depp and Peter Jackson, who funded their legal defence. The men were also the subject of three Paradise Lost HBO documentaries by Joe Berlinger and Bruce Sinofsky.

Deadline covered the documentaries and the trio’s release extensively at the time. The story was also captured in Devil’s Knot, a 2013 fiction feature directed by Atom Egoyan and starring Colin Firth and Reese Witherspoon. The Arkansas Supreme Court reopened the murder case and ordered fresh testing of the DNA found at the crime scene in 2024. The case is still ongoing.

#3346. Windows Laptops Just Closed a Major Gap With the MacBook Neo

To say the MacBook Neo disrupted the laptop market would be an understatement. When the Neo dropped, former Apple CEO Tim Cook said Apple had its best-ever launch week for first-time Mac customers, and the company is reportedly planning on doubling the MacBook's sales for 2027. It's not hard to see why the MacBook Neo is such a hit: Apple is offering the essential Mac experience at a fantastic price point. You no longer need to spend $1,000 or more for a MacBook, so long as you're okay making some sacrifices to get there—which, it seems, many customers are.

While the MacBook Neo has been a boon for Apple and Apple fans alike, I can only imagine the stress it brought to PC manufacturers—especially those with budget or midrange machines. Windows PCs have long won the price war against Apple. While MacBooks have their passionate customers, buyers looking for the best value have had to weigh expensive Apple laptops against many far cheaper options from companies like Dell, HP, ASUS, and Lenovo. But with the Neo, suddenly a MacBook was competing in this space, and well.

Part of the issue for PC manufacturers was Apple's control over its own ecosystem. Unlike most PC makers, which only produce the hardware for each machine, Apple makes both the hardware and the software for its MacBook lineup. As such, the company has the advantage of optimizing that hardware. It can design macOS to run more efficiently on weaker hardware, in a way that companies like Dell or ASUS can't. You might be comparing the MacBook Neo against a Windows laptop with similar specs, or even better specs, but because Microsoft makes Windows, not the laptop manufacturer, it's possible the Neo ends up with the better overall experience. While that might still be the case, Microsoft may have just closed that gap in a meaningful way.

This week, Microsoft announced key upgrades to memory-management efficiency, particularly for machines with 8GB of RAM. This is the amount of memory the MacBook Neo has, as well as many budget and midrange Windows laptops. That's not much memory for 2026, regardless of platform, but Apple seems to have squeezed a lot out of it for the Neo. Now, Microsoft may have just done the same for PCs, as Windows is reportedly 20% more responsive, with 40% faster multitasking.

In its blog post, Microsoft highlighted improvements that users with 8 GB of RAM can expect from Windows going forward. First, Microsoft says it focused on better utilizing the RAM your machine already has. The company compares its memory management to a desk: Anything on the "desk" is stored in RAM; anything in your "drawer" is stored in your drive. As you use your PC, Windows used to move more of your apps and tabs to your drawer to free up more RAM for other things, meaning you'd need to reload those items whenever you returned to them. Going forward, the company says that Windows can keep up to 2GB more of your active data in RAM instead of moving it to slower storage elsewhere. That means apps and tabs should refresh less frequently when you leave and return to them.

Microsoft also says that small actions should be faster across the board. When you open the Start menu, search across your PC, right-click, open Settings, launch the Snipping Tool, and open File Explorer, those actions may be up to 20% faster than they were in January. Microsoft Edge may open up to 33% faster, while Teams can enable Efficiency Mode by default on 8 GB machines, which means it can launch up to 20% faster too. Microsoft put together an interesting stress test to compare multitasking performance between today and January. It opened 20 tabs in Edge, a 4K video, large Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files, then Outlook and File Explorer, all without closing any windows. That experience was 40% faster following this latest update.

Microsoft says it also improved the memory efficiency in its apps: The company claims it reduced committed-memory growth by up to 900 MB, and saved up to 360 MB in RAM across Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook. That extends to third-party apps as well: Microsoft says that WhatsApp has double-digit memory improvement now. Widgets also only load when you open the app, which saves 200 MB of RAM when the app is closed, while Edge tabs go inactive after 15 minutes instead of two hours.

Microsoft isn't making these upgrades in a vacuum. Hardware costs, particularly for RAM, have skyrocketed in the age of AI. Microsoft knows that people are likely going to hold onto existing hardware for longer than they usually do, or that they'll opt for less-expensive configurations, including, perhaps, machines with 8 GB of RAM.

PCMag's Chris Hoffman was adamant before this latest Windows update that buyers should steer clear of PCs with 8 GB of RAM. Now, he's pulling back a bit. In his testing, Hoffman noticed improvements when multitasking on an 8 GB PC when compared to similar tests from months ago. He could run multiple Chrome tabs, a Microsoft Word window, and Spotify without bogging down the computer much. Hoffman isn't a lightweight user, so he still wouldn't personally choose an 8 GB machine, but he admits, "If I were an average PC buyer looking for a reasonable desktop experience and could save hundreds of dollars by opting for 8GB of RAM, I might be happy with the performance."

To that point, I think this new Windows update makes 8 GB PCs competitive, especially against the MacBook Neo. We'll still need direct comparisons to know how well this new Windows experience holds up across the board, but these updates are promising. Users with 8 GB machines just got a free, valuable update overnight; new customers can opt for a more affordable PC without feeling like performance will take a nosedive just because they opened one too many Edge tabs.

As Hoffman says, 8 GB of RAM is not ideal for any user looking for serious multitasking or professional workflows, regardless of whether they choose a Mac or PC. But for the average computer customer looking for a solid machine without breaking the bank, I no longer see the Neo as necessarily the default choice. After all, Apple has slowly raised its price, too, from $599 to $699. If you're platform-agnostic, or even prefer Windows to macOS, these updates from Microsoft are quite promising. If you're in the market, check out PCMag's excellent list of budget laptop recommendations.

#3345. Meet the 20 first-place apps from RevenueCat’s Shipaton 2026

A cozy habit tracker, a smarter snippet library, and a rooster that wants you out of bed: this year’s Shipaton winners offer plenty of new apps to explore.

RevenueCat’s annual app-building competition drew 3,985 project submissions in 2026, according to its winner announcement. Across the 20 first-place categories, developers tackled everyday frustrations, built inventive games, and found new ways to connect people.

You can get a look at every first place winner below, and read RevenueCat’s full winner announcement for every more.

Keeping a routine is easier when there’s something to look forward to. Mio pairs self-care and habit tracking with a pixel companion that grows as you make progress. Check off habits, earn coins, and unlock new companions and collectibles, with friends and groups adding a social reason to keep going.

Mio took Shipaton’s Grand Prize, with RevenueCat highlighting its revenue and growth in a crowded habit-tracking market.

That dog you met on your morning walk can become part of your collection. Boop identifies cats and dogs and turns their photos into stickers for a digital book, giving pet lovers a playful reason to pay attention to the animals around them.

Creator Taiwo Omisore’s “100 Boops” challenge took the app into the real world, where printed pet portraits and conversations with owners helped shape the product. That hands-on approach earned Boop first place in #BuildInPublic.

If you have fond memories of futuristic arcade racers, Nitelore has a familiar appeal: hovering vehicles, neon tracks, and plenty of speed. Chase your own ghost in time trials, take on combat races, or compete online.

Free tracks offer a starting point, while paid unlocks and daily and weekly challenges give players more to explore. RevenueCat’s Best Game judges singled out the art direction, effects, and haptics.

Explaining how you see color can be surprisingly difficult. See as Me: Colorblind makes that conversation visual, using a split-screen camera to compare different types and degrees of color blindness. A shareable link lets someone else see the comparison without installing the app.

Developer Javier Jiménez drew on his own experience with protanopia. That personal perspective helped the app earn the RevenueCat Peace Prize.

Clucky’s rooster is determined to get you out of bed. Turning off an alarm can require solving a problem, moving around, or finding an object, bringing a little friction to the temptation to snooze.

Its personality runs through the entire interface, including a time picker that uses the rooster’s scrolling eyes and yellow beak. That consistent character, animation, and attention to detail earned Clucky the RevenueCat Design Award.

Adversary starts with a familiar challenge: flip cards and find matching pairs. The catch is a hidden Danger card with no matching partner. Reveal it, and an ad becomes part of the board you’re trying to remember.

That idea earned Niv Ben-porath’s game the Catvertising Award. Players can continue with ads after an initial ad-free period, or choose a permanent unlock that removes ads and adds difficulty options.

Put a few phones on the table, and Bubble Games turns their screens into a shared game board. Objects move between devices as friends compete in minigames, including a virtual hot potato.

Built by four software engineering students at Université Laval, the Next Gen Award winner uses the phones people already have to create a shared activity. Its Shipaton submission includes ten minigames. The winner announcement links to the Android release on Google Play.

1st place • HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money)

GRIDLOCK takes a game everyone knows and adds up to four players, online rooms, and eleven special moves. The result offers more ways to disrupt an opponent’s plans than the familiar three-by-three board.

Its HAMM Award win recognizes how the business model fits the game: a shared Credits currency connects rewarded ads, optional packs, and a subscription, while core modes remain free. Players can choose the option that fits how often they play.

1st place • Influencer Award – Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen

Just Add begins with a craving. Type what you feel like eating, describe it aloud, or take a photo, and the app suggests three meals built around it, adding protein, fiber, and healthy fats to round out the plate.

Shopping support, hands-free cooking, and remembered preferences help carry the idea through to dinner. The winner of Abbey’s Kitchen’s nutrition challenge also impressed judges with a dinner-host feature that accounts for other people’s preferences.

1st place • Influencer Award – Productivity: Christopher Lawley

The reply you send every week, the PDF you keep hunting for, and the image you paste repeatedly can all live in SnipStash. It organizes reusable text, images, and files across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with a keyboard, Mac quick palette, hotkeys, and Shortcuts bringing them within reach.

Private iCloud sync connects the library across devices. Its speed and native interface helped it win Christopher Lawley’s productivity challenge.

1st place • Influencer Award – Career Coaching: Leadership Heather

Knowing what you want to say and saying it aloud are different things. Rehearse – Hard Conversations gives you an AI counterpart to practice with before a difficult workplace discussion.

Choose from 33 prepared scenarios or bring your own situation, then review feedback on clarity, empathy, assertiveness, and structure. A prep card helps you take the useful points into the real conversation. The app won Leadership Heather’s career-coaching challenge for its focused, straightforward approach.

1st place • Influencer Award – Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming

You see a game in a short video, mean to look it up later, and forget its name. Game Magnet lets you share the clip to identify the games and save them to your backlog.

Processing happens in the background, with a notification when the result is ready. Shelves, ratings, and ranked lists help organize what comes next. The app won Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming’s challenge by making discovery and keeping track of games easier.

1st place • Influencer Award – Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice

FeelGood: Movement Menu starts with a short check-in about your energy, available time, and how you want to feel. It then offers a small menu of movement, with an appetizer, main, and optional sides.

The options span yoga, Pilates, strength, walking, stretching, and breathing. Rest is part of the experience, too. Yusra Salam and Ameena Malik’s app won Simone Sharice’s yoga and fitness challenge, with judges praising its calm, inviting design.

BoatBrawl brings arcade boat battles to a group of up to eight players. Steer, fire, and scramble through interactive arenas, with bots and shared-screen play offering more ways to join in.

Rehaan Cubes and Ashwin K M used Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform to bring the game across phones and computers, including iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, and the web. Its smooth browser play helped it take JetBrains’ Ship Kotlin Everywhere award.

Trazo: Golf Ball Tracer adds a ball-flight line to your own golf videos. Select the ball twice to start, and the processing runs on the phone.

Julian Praest’s app won Most Viral App for the way its team introduced the product through organic content. Golf humor and practical advice set up the tracer reveal, making the finished video part of the pitch. For golfers, the appeal is simple: make the shot easier to follow when you share it.

One Piece Card Game collectors know that similar-looking cards can be very different finds. Grandfolio helps identify artwork variants, manage duplicates, and track collection prices and progress.

The Best App for Galaxy winner impressed judges with layouts that adapt to folded, tabletop, and open-screen use. There’s an App Store release for Apple users, too, making this a relevant discovery even if your collection starts on an iPhone.

Let’s Get Support by 3Dadz is designed for partners, parents, and friends affected by someone else’s addiction. Check-ins, journaling, boundary-setting tools, and local resources give those supporters a place to focus on their own needs.

Joshua Burgess and Aaryn B. built the app from community conversations in British Columbia, using Replit to turn the idea into a live product. It won Replit’s Idea to Income award. The announcement links to its Android release.

PoquitoTalk: Bocas del Toro turns English into local Spanish voice notes for WhatsApp and helps translate the replies. The recipient doesn’t need to install the app, keeping the conversation in a tool people already use.

Creator Dorien Van den Abbeele drew on years of life in Bocas del Toro. Its Growth Loop Award recognizes extensive growth experiments and an honest account of what the measurements could show. The announcement links to Google Play.

Parky! combines wait times, dining availability, and memories from Disney and Universal visits. Built by former Disney Cast Member Chase Van Derrick, it aims to offer useful help throughout a park day.

Dining alerts can become conversations on the Lock Screen, where you can ask about another time or restaurant. Alongside queue Live Activities and recap messages, those interactive notifications helped Parky! win the Keep Them Coming Back Award.

In Your Own Words offers short, real-world speaking scenarios and feedback on pace, hesitation, and filler words. Speech analysis takes place on the phone, giving users a way to practice the words before they need them.

Natasha Wilson’s app won the Funnel Vision Award for connecting a web quiz, a relevant practice deck, and a web purchase that unlocks access in the app. The introduction to the product begins before the download.

Friendpire turns the idea of a board-game night with friends into a shared hex-tile world. Gather resources, build farms and docks, and grow an empire together. RevenueCat employee Erik MacInnis built the game to make it easier to stay connected with friends who rarely find time to play.

Friendpire won the separate Conflict of Interest Award, which was open to RevenueCat and sponsor employees and judged by Shipaton participants. It is included here as an optional sidebar and is not part of the 20 first-place count above.

From a useful tool for the workday to a game for your next night in, Shipaton’s winners show how much can come from taking an idea all the way to a shipped app. Explore the winners above, or browse RevenueCat’s full announcement for more apps from the competition.

#3344. ‘SNL’ Makes Grok Do “Epic Vulgar Roast” Of Elon Musk On ‘Weekend Update’: “The Worst Thing South Africa Has Ever Done”

Elon Musk has returned to Saturday Night Live, through Jeremy Culhane‘s hilarious impression, to give a postmortem of the midterm elections.

As “Weekend Update” co-anchor Colin Jost noted, Musk has been in the news after he wasted half a billion dollars on backing candidates who lost, but the trillionaire disagreed with that take.

“No, I’m in the news because my car did a flip! My car did a flip, remember? It was like a frickin’ Hot Wheel,” Culhane’s Musk told Jost. “But I was like, totally chill. I was like, ‘Thug life!’ Imagine?”

As Jost reminded him, most of the candidates Musk backed lost their elections. “Nice! That was like an epic roast of me. Most vulgar. You know, that’s what I call an epic vulgar roast. And it’s time for a pounding,” said Culhane before initiating an awkward fist bump with Jost. Watch on Deadline

Following “another epic vulgar roast from Colin Jost, my poorest friend,” Musk revealed Epic Vulgar Roast is actually “AI Grok’s most epic hardcore feature. It’s so vulgar and hilariously funny.”

Musk told Grok to do an “epic vulgar roast” of him as an example, to which the robotic voice generated, “Elon Musk, you’re the worst thing South Africa has ever done. When you’re on TV, it feels like an episode of Hate on the Spectrum. Maybe if you have 100 more kids, one of them will talk to you.”

The sketch comes after Musk attempted to brush off his election losses with an attempt at a joke. “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now. Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” he wrote on X.

In addition to Druski’s SNL hosting debut — marking the first content creator without a current movie or TV show to host the sketch comedy show — The Strokes served as musical guest for a fifth time on this weekend’s episode.

#3343. I teach people over 50 to build strength and mobility — here's 3 beginner-friendly exercises I always start with

As a trainer, fitness editor and all-round fitness nerd, I get a lot of joy from seeing the needle move in my own training, but also with my clients. And to set them up for success, we always work on foundational, functional strength and movement patterns — think squats, presses, deadlifts and pulls — and basic mobility before we move on to anything else.

That's because if you can't master the basics, the loads shouldn't increase and your variations should wait, unless you have an injury or health condition which prevents you from performing certain moves, of course.

I teach a lot of people in their 50s and 60s, and while some of these clients love the gym, others want to exercise at home with little gym equipment, so that's when I use a "back to basics" approach, which is exactly what these beginner-friendly exercises are.

Take a look below if you need some inspiration and let me know your thoughts — and you results — in the comments below.

Here they are. You can use the best kettlebells or dumbbells, or light plates if you prefer.

Normally, I'd have clients learn the overhead press first, then move straight to the Arnold press variation. Why? Because this press uses rotation as you lift, meaning all three of the shoulder heads get stronger, making your routine a bit more well-rounded without having to do more.

You still build pressing power and work your upper chest, upper back and triceps, but with a little twist as you go.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Presses are very functional, too, because they mimic lifting something overhead, like a heavy box, or putting your child on your shoulders. This strength exercise can be loaded gradually to become more challenging, and you can slowly improve core stability and pressing power using just a set of weights.

I'm not against gym machines, but you'll build much more stability and work your core muscles harder using free weights. That's because you don't have the controlled support of a machine to guide you, and this allows you to learn from the very start how to control the load using both sides of your body.

In theory, working with kettlebells and dumbbells should reduce the likelihood of imbalances developing because you must lift evenly with your left and right sides. This is known as unilateral training, and it's one of my favorite ways to build balance and coordination in the body.

Enter the front rack squat. You can load one side of the body or use two weights racked at your shoulders with your elbows pressed high to shelve the weights. You'll need to brace your stomach for balance and sit your hips back to achieve a deep squat, working your legs hard as squats do, but also engaging your upper body with the load at your shoulders.

Focus on an upright torso and press through your feet and legs to stand each rep.

Finally, we take a look at controlled core and pulling power.

The renegade row can be performed on your knees or in full plank position, which engages your whole body, including your arms, shoulders, glutes, quads, hamstrings and chest, as well as your core. From here, row one weight at a time toward your back pocket, working the back and biceps.

During renegade rows, you'll be positioned in a three-point hold, which means your body must work hard to resist rotation; developing anti-rotation strength will build a stronger, more stable core.

Aim to lift lighter than you'd normally go for a row, then build gradually. Keep your hips square and press out of your shoulders with your hips aligned with the rest of your body. Pull for the count of one, then lower for the count of two or three seconds.

Resistance training as a whole is your anti-aging weapon for healthier joints and stronger ligaments, tendons, bones and muscles as you get older. This is especially true for women, as hormonal shifts and metabolism can take a dive later in life, so the more lean muscle mass you have, the faster your resting metabolism is, and the more protected your body will be.

I recommend starting with 8-12 reps per move per side of the body for 3-4 sets. You can add weight every few weeks, but if you don't have equipment, adjust the reps, sets, or tempo. I recommend at least 2-3 strength sessions per week, mixing a variety of movements to target the major muscle groups every few months to keep your body stimulated and engaged.

If you experience pain at any time, stop and rest. If you're working with an injury or health condition, I recommend seeking advice before starting these exercises.

Sam Hopes is a level 3 qualified trainer, a level 2 Reiki practitioner and fitness editor at Tom's Guide. She is also currently undertaking her Yoga For Athletes training course.

Sam has written for various fitness brands and websites over the years and has experience across brands at Future, such as Live Science, Fit&Well, Coach, and T3.

Having coached at fitness studios like F45 and Virgin Active and taken on both 1:1 and group, Sam now primarily teaches outdoor bootcamps, bodyweight, and kettlebells.

She also coaches mobility and flexibility classes several times a week.

#3342. Walmart Will Have Three Major Shopping Events This Holiday Season

If you're thinking of picking up any big-ticket items soon—whether for yourself or as a gift for someone on your list— I would advise you to wait until you see what retailers have in store for the holiday sales season, which will kick off in earnest in mid-November. Walmart is the first major retailer to announce its Black Friday and Cyber Monday plan for 2026, and they actually involve three major shopping events between now and the December holidays.

As it did in 2025, Walmart will hold three sales between Nov. 12 and Dec. 2, as outlined in a recent press release. The sales will be both online and in-store, and will target a mix of Walmart+ members and general shoppers.

The events will take place on three different dates:

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 1: Nov. 12–15

Available online and in stores starting at 6 a.m. local time

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access beginning online at 12:01 a.m. ET on November 12

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 2: Nov. 23–29

Online only: Nov. 23 starting at 12:01 a.m. ET

Online and in stores: Nov. 27 starting at 6 a.m. local time

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access online beginning Nov. 23 at 12:01 a.m. ET

Walmart's Cyber Monday Deals Event: Nov. 30-Dec. 2

Walmart says that you can expect discounts on electronics, toys, fashion, beauty, home goods, gifts, and everyday essentials. Although the company doesn't provide much in the way of specifics in its press release, last year's sales included discounts on TCL TVs, Dyson vacuums, Dreo appliances, and toys from LEGO.

Walmart already has plenty of good deals out early. You don't need to wait for the official sale to start to find some products going for their lowest prices ever. Here are some of the best ones I've found so far:

The holiday season will see major sales from the same list of retailers that compete for your dollars throughout the year—namely, Best Buy, Target, and Amazon. Each will have its own version of Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales. So far, only Walmart has revealed its plans.

In short, yes. Though they aren't quite as impactful as they once were, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales offer discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Whether it's a major purchase you've been saving up for or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts, especially on items like appliances and electronics. Last year's sales included categories such as tech, home improvement, and fitness.

Black Friday used to be when major retailers offered their best deals on expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Now, however, the distinction is almost meaningless: Every major retailer offers sales on both days, which means the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers to monitor the deals, and refer to our Black Friday coverage, where we do all the searching, curating, and price tracking for you.

#3341. Next year’s iPhone Pro redesign gets new update from leaker

Apple reportedly has a big redesign coming to next year’s iPhone Pro models, timed for the iPhone’s 20th anniversary. The latest leak about the design reveals that the dream of a cutout-free display may remain a dream for now.

Yesterday Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station outlined three new iPhone models coming in early 2027: iPhone 18e, iPhone 18, and iPhone Air 2.

His main focus was on the iPhone 18, which is expected to get two Pro-inspired upgrades.

In a follow-up post though, replying to another Weibo user’s question, the leaker addressed a key design question regarding next fall’s iPhone Pro models.

Apple is rumored to be working on a big redesign timed for the iPhone’s 20th anniversary. It will reportedly feature a quad-curved display that wraps around the edges of the device for a visually bezel-free look.

Early rumors indicated the device could also drop the Dynamic Island for a truly all-glass display, with no cutouts.

The Duo2 will also have faceID and will steal the show. Who wants curved glass on all sides of the phone? We all remember how that went for Galaxy Edge phones.

But according to Digital Chat Station, that’s not happening after all.

After being asked if the ‘iPhone 20 Pro Max’ will have a Dynamic Island still, or feature a hole-free display, the leaker confirmed the display will still have holes. Thus, it will retain the Dynamic Island cutout.

It’s unclear if the Dynamic Island will be the same size as that of iPhone 18 Pro, but since the device is expected to have Face ID, that’s highly likely.

Does the inclusion of a display cutout change your interest in the iPhone 20 Pro at all? Let us know in the comments.

#3340. ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is King Of The Global Weekend Box Office With $63M, Towers Over ‘Ramayana’s $55M+ WW Opening

SUNDAY AM: Toho’s lizard had no plans to be undone by a Hindu deity in a fight at the global box office as Godzilla Minus Zero roared $63M WW over Prime Focus Studio and Sony’s Ramayana: Rise of a Legend‘s $55.7M global, the bulk of that gross in India.

Ramayana had good fortune in Europe, where we hear it was No. 1 in the UK and Australia, trampling the Godzilla and Ghidorah, but the monsters reigned in Mexico in the No. 1 spot and most of Latin America (however not Brazil where a local comedy title was No. 1). Godzilla Minus Zero has been raging in Japan where since its Tuesday, Godzilla Day, it has collected 2.7 billion yen or $17M. There will be more updates on Godzilla Minus Zero tomorrow. Related Stories News 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Is A Box Office Hero With $32M Live-Action Foreign-Language Opening Record - Saturday AM Update News 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Stomping To $60M+ WW Opening, Posts Massive First Day In Japan; Will 'Ramayana' Upset The Lizard? - Box Office Preview

Ramayana: Part One collected the bulk of its global in India with $32M, followed by a 4-day take of $12.2M in the U.S. and $11.5M in 37 remaining foreign territories handled by Sony. A press note reads that the first part of a $420M-$500M production is the most watched movie in the world over the Diwali holiday with 11M tickets sold, but there’s nothing to support that stat, so just note it for now. Ramayana: Rise of a Legend was booked on over 10,000 screens in north of 130 countries in 17 dubbed languages. Watch on Deadline

For all the pom pom waving here on Ramayana, Lord knows how this movie makes it all its money back because by Hollywood accounting ledger standards a $55.7M global opening on a movie that costs roughly $250M is considered a flop. However, this movie is expected to leg out in India to potentially a 4x or more multiple. Also, the marketing spend on these movies are very thrifty, often as low as $1M worldwide (not counting India). Word of mouth is very easy to spread on Indian features given how close-knit the communities are around the world. And Ramayana here is akin to making a movie about Jesus Christ or even on the level of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. Also, there’s a question by sources with knowledge of India’s motion picture industry whether Ramayana cost as much as it did; the VFX reportedly handled by the filmmaker in-house.

Similar to Christmas Eve, Indian audiences head to religious services on the days before Diwali with moviegoing increasing thereafter.

Prince Rama broke local market opening records for a film from India, including the United Kingdom ($3.0M), Thailand($550K), the Netherlands ($240K) and South Africa ($75K).

Ramayana is the second biggest opening for an Indian movie in North America at $12.2M behind Dhurandhar: The Revenge which debuted to $14M back in March.

Other top-performing markets include the United Arab Emirates ($2.2M), Australia ($1.9M), Germany ($625K) and Nepal ($500K).

Upcoming market releases for Ramayana include Indonesia (Nov 11), Hong Kong (Nov 12), Mexico (Nov 12), Central Asia (Nov 12), Brazil (Nov 19), Italy (Nov 19), Ukraine (Nov 19), Hungary (Nov 19), Poland (Nov 20), Argentina (Nov 26), Central America (Nov 26), Colombia (Nov 26), Ecuador (Nov 26), Peru (Nov 26) and Czechia (Nov 26).

With a fight like this between a Prince and reptiles, it’s Imax who benefits the most, collecting $29M combined from largely both movies around the globe.

Godzilla Minus Zero in Imax reaped $21.3M, repping 34% of the pic’s worldwide opening and getting a new record for the biggest Imax global opening for a Japanese film. As we told, PLFs and Imax combined counted a 74% share of the pic’s $31.6M opening. Imax alone in North America repped 40% of the weekend’s ticket sales or $12.7M at 429 screens. Overseas, Godzilla Minus Zero played on 421 screens across 64 markets or $8.6M with Japan leading the way with $4M — easily the highest Imax opening ever in the market.

“With Godzilla Minus Zero, Takashi Yamazaki and our friends at Toho have delivered a tremendous feat of filmmaking with arresting visuals that somehow top its predecessor; we are proud to call this the first Filmed For IMAX release from Japan and delighted fans are overwhelmingly choosing to experience it in on our screens,” said Rich Gelfond, CEO of IMAX. “Japan continues to be among the biggest success stories across our global footprint, and we know this historic success will only create further opportunities for filmmaker partnership and network growth in this thriving marketing for cinema.”

The Nitesh Tiwari-directed Ramayana saw $6M from Imax, repping 11% of the title’s global weekend, delivering the biggest global Imax opening ever for an Indian film. The Filmed for Imax release saw $2M in India, which was the biggest Imax opening ever in the market. There was another $1.4M in Imax box office from 32 international markets outside India. North America delivered $2.5M from 53 screens, accounting for a strong 20% of the film’s stateside bow.

There seems to be shade being thrown around Warner Bros Pictures Animation’s The Cat in the Hat with its high $80M+ production cost after a 10% co-financing (just under $90M) from Domain and a $30.5M global start. It’s not fizzling, it’s just starting off slow, and thank the box office gods the Bill Hader-voiced movie got to a $20.5M start stateside as many worried it would fall into the teens. The pic has a staggered rollout to take advantage of territories during the year-end holidays.

Territory grosses weren’t wild like the cat himself with $10M from 60 territories including Mexico ($1.1M, lower than Elio‘s $1.3M), Italy ($1M, higher than Elio‘s $872K), Spain ($999K, similar to Elio), China ($663K way lower than Elio‘s $2.2M start), Brazil ($541K, lower than Elio‘s $771K), Colombia ($535K), Poland ($422K), UAE ($312K), Ecuador ($280K), Saudi Arabia ($278K), Korea ($220K) and Kazakhstan ($189K).

Why not bigger, particularly stateside? Unlike the Grinch and the Lorax, the Cat in the Hat, despite being Dr. Seuss’ Mickey Mouse if you will, is a tricky character. You would have thought a live-action Mike Myers version back in 2003, after Universal’s 2000 hit The Grinch with Jim Carrey, wouldn’t have been reported as a bomb despite crossing over $100M in North America. This movie a la a Peanuts movie seemed geared toward a younger-skewing audience, and point on, that’s exactly correct with close to 60% under the age of 9 years of age. Beyond a certain age, this isn’t cool, particularly for an older crowd. Also, there was something in the materials that made this feel safe, and not anarchistic rebellion in its comedic tone a la Illumination/20th Century Fox’s 2012 mega-hit The Lorax which opened to $70.2M in North America and ended its run at $214M+ domestic, and close to $349M WW. That movie, to this day, still has Gen Z social media content creators like Juicy Jacob still impersonating the character and delighting fans in public.

Searchlight’s Martin McDonagh-written and directed spy comedy caper Wild Horse Nine galloped to $12.6M around the globe in its opening with $6M domestic and $6.6M from 29 territories. The movie has yet to opening in Germany, Spain, Japan, Argentina and smaller Euro and Asian countries.

At $6M, that’s the biggest opening for a McDonagh movie in North America. The John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell movie was the top U.S. movie in New Zealand and the second highest MPA title in Australia, Korea, Belgium, Finland, Netherlands, Georgia and Chile. In NZ, Australia and Korea, the pic’s opening is above McDonagh’s The Banshees of Inisherin. Weekend comes were UK ($2M), Italy ($1M), France ($700K), Australia ($700K), Netherlands ($500K), Greece ($300K), Belgium ($200K) and Korea ($200K).

McDonagh’s highest grossing movie ever at the box office is his multi Oscar winner Three Billboards Outside Ebbing Missouri which counts $162.7M WW with $108.2M from international alone.

Other shoutouts at the international B.O.:

Black Bear’s Wicker saw a $7M international weekend with $3.35M in North America (-23%) and $3.7M abroad for a running global cume of $29M ($19.9M from U.S./Canada). Wicker opened in five new markets, bringing its release to 14 international territories to date: UK/Ireland, France, Netherlands, Belgium, Spain, Greece, Israel, India, West Indies, Australia, New Zealand, CIS, Ukraine, and Philippines. The grand running foreign cume is $9.15M.

UK’s second weekend posted $1.5M, -33%, at 719 theaters with a total of $5.7M so far. Australia bowed to $918K ahead of Wild Horse Nine, but behind Ramayana and Godzilla Minus Zero. Pic’s start in Oz is +43% ahead of Poor Things, +24% ahead of Wicked Little Letters, and 10% ahead of Sense and Sensibility. Netherlands’ third frame added $109K, -29%, from 81 locations for a running cume of $632K.

Universal began rolling out George Michael – The Faith Tour with $2.1M in 35 territories at 2,060 locations. UK minted $1.3M at 620 screens. The first two days far outgrossed the total runs of previous George Michael and Wham!-adjacent event cinema titles Wham! 10 Days in China and George Michael Freedom Uncut. The overall weekend result is more than double the expansion weekend of Moonage Daydream, more than 3x Becoming Led Zeppelin and in line with Renaissance: Beyonce. Netherlands with $200K debuted in the No. 7 spot, with Imax repping 34% of the weekend. That take is ahead of Metallica: 72 Seasons, more than double Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger and more than 3x Becoming Led Zeppelin. Italy saw $200K in No. 10 above EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert. Denmark was $106K No. 3 in line with Moonage Daydream, above Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger and more than 4x Becoming Led Zeppelin. Poland was $70K above EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert with Belgium posting a No. 8 bow with $61K from a 4-day weekend.

#3339. Report: Apple reduces employees’ AI token allowances as Ternus moves to cut costs

Bloomberg reports that Apple has begun reducing employees’ daily AI spending limits, with some engineers seeing their allowances cut from $300 to $200, and further reductions planned across multiple teams. Here are the details.

Over the past year, tokenmaxxing, the practice of consuming as many AI tokens as possible, often as a measure of productivity, took over Silicon Valley, with companies such as Meta even introducing internal leaderboards, some unofficial, ranking employees by their AI token usage.

Tokenmaxxing emerged alongside improvements in AI agents’ coding capabilities, as tools such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor became increasingly popular among software developers.

Unsurprisingly, companies soon began to rein in token usage as the rising costs of AI tools raised questions about whether the productivity gains justified the expense. Just recently, Accenture reportedly reduced its centrally funded Claude allowance to just $29 per employee per month, requiring any additional spending to be covered by individual projects or teams.

And while there hadn’t been reports of disproportionate token usage from engineers and other employees at Apple, Bloomberg reported today that the company is also looking to rein in employees’ AI spending as part of CEO John Ternus’ broader cost-cutting efforts.

Last month, Apple quietly lowered the daily spending cap for some engineers using AI models to $200 from $300, according to people with knowledge of the change. The company is now planning further cuts for some engineering teams, potentially reducing their daily allowances to as little as $100, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private.

Many groups outside of engineering already face a $100 daily cap, but Apple has considered reducing that limit to as little as $25 for some teams, the people said. Employees who require higher allowances to perform their jobs will be able to seek exemptions from senior leadership.

It is not immediately clear which tools are affected by the new spending limits. However, Bloomberg reports that Apple employees have access to several AI services, including Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s ChatGPT, and Google’s Gemini. Some teams are also being encouraged to use cheaper AI models or models that run locally on their devices to reduce costs.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman had previously said that Apple was heavily reliant on Anthropic’s AI models for its internal operations, describing the company as essentially “running on Anthropic,” despite its partnership with Google to power Siri.

That came a few months after then-CEO Tim Cook encouraged employees to make greater use of AI in their daily work during an all-hands meeting, saying, “All of us are using AI in a significant way already, and we must use it as a company as well.”

$200-$300 per day is a pretty high amount. There are certainly people and tasks that can effectively put that many tokens to efficient use, but my guess is that most people bumping those limits could be more efficient in their use.

You’re going to always have that one person who complains about the budget but is out there making small code changes running Fable on max. These blanket token budgets typically seek to limit damage from those types while those that can make a case for why they need more budget typically get it.

Back to today’s report, Bloomberg says employee reactions to the new spending limits have been mixed. According to its sources, “few workers were using their full $300 daily allowances,” while others “see the reductions as a sign of broader cost cutting, adding to concerns about potential layoffs.”

Interestingly, the cuts come as Apple’s overall spending continues to rise. Earlier this week, Apple reported its fiscal Q4 2026 earnings, bringing its fiscal year to a close with R&D expenses up 32% to $45.8 billion, driven in part by higher infrastructure and AI costs.

Bloomberg notes that it remains unclear how much Apple will actually save through the new restrictions, particularly since some employees weren’t using their full allowances to begin with.

#3338. Sony Wants to Give You Up to $400 for Your PS5

Companies usually want you to buy something from them. They might cut prices to make their products more enticing, or introduce perks and upgrades to make stagnant prices (or even price hikes) more appealing. But rarely do I see companies encourage customers to sell their products.

Such is the case with Sony and its PlayStation console. This week, the company began reaching out to some customers with an odd prompt: Rather than buy a new PS5 or PS5 Pro, you can sell your existing PS5 console for up to $400. There are stipulations there, of course: Your console needs to be in good working order, and, apparently, come with two controllers—even though Sony only includes one in the box. The price could also fluctuate depending on your console model, storage capacity, and included accessories. But, still, the company says it'll help you net up to $400 for your existing PS5.

It's a bizarre deal, especially when you consider who you're trading your console to. Sony isn't necessarily accepting trade-ins itself. Instead, it's partnering with BackMarket. The thing is, you can trade in your PS5 directly through BackMarket and get a better value than Sony is offering through its direct link. When I try to trade in my standard PS5 with one controller, BackMarket offers $435, $35 more than Sony's highest offer. If I add a second controller to that deal, BackMarket bumps up the total to $455.

You might also be wondering why Sony would do this. Not only is it weird for a company to encourage you to sell one of its products, but the PS5 is about to have a big moment. Grand Theft Auto VI is finally about to launch, and it'll likely be one of the biggest video game launches, if not the biggest video game launch, of all time. Why, then, would Sony encourage users to jump ship?

While Sony doesn't say, the answer likely has to do with how expensive it is to pick up a PS5 right now. Even though the console launched back in 2020, units are few and far between, jacking the price up to unreasonable levels. Sony raised international prices due to tariffs last year, but the current shortage is more probably tied to the ongoing memory crisis that's putting a strain on all tech, including game consoles. A new PS5 on Amazon will easily cost you over $800. If you want to find a PS5 Pro, don't be surprised to find it well over $1,000. Sony likely wants players who aren't using their consoles to sell them, so that active players (who will also buy games like GTA VI) will pick them up. It's not just Sony, either: Microsoft has been offering similar deals to inactive Xbox gamers this year.

If Sony reached out to you directly, you can take advantage of the deal without issue—just click the link in the email. But if you never received such an offer, you still have options. For one, that BackMarket deal is live for anyone. That links takes you to the deal for the standard PS5, but you can also head to this link to enter the info for your specific PS5 model. GameStop, of course, will happily take your PS5 off your hands, but it doesn't seem as generous as BackMarket. Right now, it seems you can get up to $275 in store credit, or $192.50 in cash for a standard PS5.

The unexpected causes of your nighttime wakeups, plus the expert-approved fixes you can action from tonight

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you've recently found yourself wide awake at 3 a.m., wondering how it's possible that yet again you're unable to sleep through the night, frustration is probably running pretty high.

It may be comforting to know you're not alone. A 2025 U.S. News and World Report survey found that, remarkably, 89% of Americans regularly wake up during the night, and 46% had a sleep goal of trying to reduce nighttime awakenings.

But help is at hand, in the form of Dr. Tom Chambers, a certified somnologist and Chief Medical Officer at Theta Sleep, Dr. Shelby Harris, a board-certified behavioral sleep medicine specialist and psychologist with BetterSleep and Hannah Shore, head of sleep science at Mattress Online.

We've spoken to these three sleep experts to explore the common causes of 3 a.m. wake-ups, the fixes that can help you sleep through the night and when you should consider speaking to your doctor. Read on to find out more...

Staring at the clock (or worse, getting a dose of bright light from your phone as you check the time) at 3 a.m. while sleep eludes you can prompt one frustrated question: 'Why?'

"There are so many reasons why we might wake up at 3 a.m. or any other time overnight. Sometimes this is completely normal, some times there are things that we can tackle head-on with changes to our sleep routines, and some are suggestive of something more serious and might mean people should speak to their doctor," ESRS-certified somnologist Dr. Chambers explains.

Below are some of the common reasons behind 3 a.m. wake-ups, as explained by the sleep experts we spoke to.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

You might be surprised to know that up briefly during the night is actually very normal, we often don't even remember it. According to research, healthy adults can wake as many as five times a night in between sleep cycles, but likely won't recall them all in the morning.

"It's not uncommon for a proportion of these wake-ups to end up being awake for a little while longer. It's when these wake-ups result in you spending hours awake ruminating on other things that this becomes an issue," Dr. Chambers says.

Some causes of nighttime awakenings are related to our sleep space and what we do in the lead up to bedtime (a.k.a our nighttime routine). Dr. Chambers delves into this:

Another cause of nighttime awakenings can be chronic stress or anxiety, which can raise baseline cortisol levels. Since our Cortisol Awakening Response (CAR) causes levels of cortisol to naturally rise in the early hours (from around 3 a.m), a stress-induced rise in your baseline cortisol levels may lead to an unwanted wake-up during this process.

"As the night goes on, your sleep naturally gets lighter, so by 3 a.m. it doesn’t take much to wake you. Stress is a major factor in this, because cortisol starts rising toward morning and can kick in early when you’re under pressure," says Dr. Harris.

Hormonal changes — including estrogen and progesterone fluctuating — that occur during perimenopause and menopause can also disrupt sleep.

"Hormonal shifts like perimenopause can bring night sweats," says Dr. Harris, while Dr. Chris Winter, a double boarded sleep specialist previously explained that other impacts of these shifts can include anxiety, temperature changes, and more fragmented sleep.

Both aging and hormonal changes can also contribute to waking at night to use the bathroom.

Shore says that 3 a.m. "is also a common time to urinate, and we find this happens more as we get older due to a reduction in certain hormones, particularly around menopause," though she adds that "changes can happen in men too, and changes to bladder efficiency."

Aging itself can also lead to disrupted nights, as according to the National Institute on Aging, shorter, light sleep in older adults can feature more nighttime awakenings.

Dr. Chambers points out that clinical sleep disorders like sleep apnea, restless leg syndrome and chronic insomnia can also all cause 3am wake-ups, and require medical advice.

"Sleep apnea is incredibly common and often undiagnosed," he says, adding that the broad symptoms of the disorder include snoring, multiple bathroom trips at night, daytime tiredness and waking up feeling unrefreshed or with a headache.

"Often patients will wake up at 3 a.m. because they've stopped breathing during their sleep. They're wide awake as their oxygen levels have dropped, triggering a fight-or-flight response," the somnologist adds.

A paper published in the journal Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment cited multiple studies that showed restless leg syndrome increased nighttime awakenings in those with the condition, while Dr. Chambers points out that "if you're regularly awake at 3 a.m., not falling asleep for a long time afterwards, and this impacts your daily life, it is almost diagnostic of clinical insomnia."

While some causes of 3 a.m. wake-ups can't be addressed by lifestyle changes alone, there are fixes to your sleep environment and nighttime routine that can help you avoid nighttime awakenings and sleep through the night more easily.

"Temperature control is very important during sleep and room temperature can have a big impact," says Dr. Chambers.

According a paper published in Frontiers for Young Minds, "a thermal environment that is either warmer or cooler than the optimal range can increase wakefulness during the night."

Research has shown that the ideal bedroom temperature for sleeping sits within the range of 65 to 70 F (18 to 21 °C).

So while it may be tempting to crank up your heating overnights as the weather gets cooler (or, in warmer months, do the same with home cooling systems), Dr. Chambers cautions against it.

"Don't leave your heating or air conditioning on all night," advises the somnologist.

It's important to "ease up on fluids in the evening," says Dr. Harris.

Although it's essential to stay hydrated, and a relaxing cup of chamomile or peppermint tea may even help your sleep, research shows that volume and timing matter.

One study explored liquid consumption two hours before bedtime, and found that all participants who drank 500ml or more experienced nocturia, and had a higher number of nighttime awakenings than the groups who drank less.

If bathroom trips are waking you up over the course of the night, one option is to give yourself a cut-off time for liquids before bed.

Dr. Chambers says that "in people who are waking up multiple times overnight to pee (and don't have a medical condition causing this) we'll sometimes suggest not drinking fluid after 7/8 p.m. in the evening."

"I think we have to understand that the 3 a.m. wake-ups are perfectly normal, especially if we are falling back to sleep within 20 minutes," Shore says.

Frustratingly, overthinking a nighttime wake-up is only likely to make it last longer.

"Often people wake up and worry that they are not falling back asleep; they watch the clock and start counting how many hours they have left. This can further drive wakefulness, meaning the body starts producing wake-promoting hormones."

She suggests having a winddown routine you can focus on instead if you wake up during the night, which gives your brain something else to focus on and allows you to relax.

This could include deep breathing exercises like the 4-7-8 technique or box breathing, both of which help to slow heart rate and activate the parasympathetic nervous system. Or you could try progressive muscle relaxation, which involves tensing and releasing muscles throughout your body and can help relax you and relieve stress and insomnia.

"It's about trying to distract your brain and switch it off again so you can fall back to sleep easily," says Shore.

A tip that follows on naturally (and is linked to) not overthinking 3 a.m. wakeups is to not focus on the time itself if you find yourself awake during the night.

"It may also help to remove any clocks from your bedroom; if you can’t see the time, then it's one less thing to worry about," says Shore.

If you can't do without a clock, or your phone, in the bedroom, Dr. Harris has a suggestion: "Turn the clock away so you’re not watching the hours tick by," she says.

"Caffeine lingers for hours, ultimately making your sleep shallow," says Dr. Harris.

Shore agrees that "Caffeine can drive wakefulness," and adds that "it is also a mild diuretic, meaning it can increase urination." She notes that people who enjoy a cup of caffeinated tea to relax before bedtime may actually be driving nighttime wakeups to take trips to the bathroom.

Shore adds that alcohol "initially has a sedative effect but then can act as a stimulant too, driving wakefulness." Indeed, multiple studies have shown that alcohol can cause wakeups during the later part of the night and early morning.

Not only that, Shore says "it can dehydrate you as well as increase urination, definitely none of the things you are wanting to do throughout the night!"

To avoid all of the above, "stop drinking alcohol three hours before bed and try to cut off caffeine by noon so they both have time to wear off," advises Dr. Harris.

"The ideal sleep environment is one that is cool, dark, and quiet," says Dr. Chambers.

To avoid middle-of-the-night wake-ups caused by noise, light and overheating, you may need to adjust a few elements of your sleep space.

"Keep pets out of the bedroom where possible," says Dr. Chambers, who also suggests "invest in some ear plugs if you're near noise. There's good evidence showing they improve sleep quality in noisy environments!"

We've discussed bedroom temperature above, but if you're someone who tends to sleep hot anyway, cooling bedding can be a wise investment. The best cooling mattresses are designed to prevent overheating at night, though a cooling mattress topper can be a more affordable way to achieve a temperate sleep.

Similarly, while blackout blinds or curtains are one of the most effective ways to avoid light pollution disrupting your sleep, they're also not cheap. A much more wallet-friendly option is a blackout sleep mask — some, like the Aura Smart Sleep Mask, even include bluetooth-controlled speakers.

Modifying your nighttime routine and sleep environment is a great way to improve sleep and minimize disturbances to your rest, but there are times when it's important to seek medical advice — particularly if you're consistently waking up at 3 a.m. for months on end.

"See a doctor if it’s happening most nights for a few months or dragging down your days. The same goes if it comes with snoring, gasping, night sweats, frequent bathroom trips or low mood," says Dr. Harris.

Shore suggests that if you notice a regular pattern of nighttime wake-ups — she says "3-4 times a week for 3-4 months," is "normally the length of time we give to say it's not just a blip or a stressful moment" — and that they are affecting your daily functioning, it's time to seek help from a medical professional.

Dr. Chambers points out that "clinical sleep disorders are incredibly common and if someone is waking up at 3 a.m. in the night every night for a long period of time they should consider seeing their doctor. At least one in four adults has a sleep disorder like insomnia, sleep apnea, or restless legs syndrome."

#3336. Apple disables Siri AI waitlist in iOS 27, with one exception

When Siri AI launched in iOS 27 earlier this fall, Apple used a waitlist to gate access. But a newly updated support document says the waitlist is no longer being used, except in “high demand” times.

If you haven’t yet enabled Siri AI on your iPhone, Apple recently made it quicker and easier to gain access.

That’s because, per updates to this support document, the company is now only using a waitlist for Siri AI in “high demand” times.

After giving instructions on how to enable Siri AI by tapping “Try Siri AI (Beta)” inside Settings, here’s what the document used to say compared to what it says now.

This will add you to a waitlist, and wait times can vary. Siri AI will begin to download automatically when your wait is complete.

Siri AI will begin to download automatically. During time of high demand, you might be added to a waitlist first, and wait times can vary.

It’s understandable that a waitlist was used initially upon iOS 27’s release. Apple needed to slowly grant access while gauging server performance. But now that we’re nearly two months into the iOS 27 rollout, it’s great that Apple is only deploying the waitlist occasionally as needed.

Have you enabled Siri AI on your iPhone? If not, what’s holding you back? Let us know in the comments.
